title: Odd-chain fatty acids as a biomarker for dietary fiber intake: a novel pathway for endogenous production from propionate
authors: Weitkunat K, Schumann S, Nickel D, Hornemann S, Petzke KJ, Schulze MB, et al.
population: Healthy adults given cellulose 30 g/day, inulin 30 g/day or propionate 6 g/day; human hepatoma cells
funder: Core budget of the German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke and German Research Foundation (DFG; KL613/18-1).
inKindSupport: Propionate (Propicum) from Flexopharm GmbH & Co. KG, cellulose (Vivapur 105) from J Rettenmaier und Soehne GmbH, inulin (Fibruline DS2) from Georg Breuer GmbH.
result: Cellulose did not change plasma phospholipid odd-chain fatty acids; inulin and propionate raised pentadecanoic acid (15:0) by about 17% (P < 0.05) and 13% (P = 0.05) and heptadecanoic acid (17:0) by 11% (P < 0.01) and 13% (P < 0.001). In hepatoma cells propionate correlated with odd-chain fatty acid levels (R2 = 0.99). The authors conclude that gut-derived propionate is used for hepatic odd-chain fatty acid synthesis in humans.
